notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after nine searches (the first three candidates). Everything else was read directly, with the kit's honest User-Agent and each site's robots.txt obeyed: the candidates' own sites, each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates and local party units' pages, the Legislative Reference Library, Wikipedia's election articles, and a few local news sites through their own search pages. No search engine was read in place of the search tool.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned by running the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) on a scratch copy of the database; each was then opened. Two more were found and read on the sites themselves: Pam Wolf's and Maggie Evers's (a voter guide's page names each address; it is not cited).

Three filed websites could not be confirmed, so no website finding is recorded for them: votejonathon.com (Jonathon Heinonen) asks all scripts to stay out in its robots.txt and was not read; olson4chisagolakes.com (Aaron Olson) shows a domain parking page today; judgejeannecochran.com (Jeanne Cochran) says only "Launching Soon".

Not read, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (403 to the script and to the reading tool), so the two judges have no official page here; the state's mn.gov pages (a Radware CAPTCHA); the City of Eagan's site (a bot check), so Gary Hansen has no official page; the City of Sartell's and Becker Township's sites (their robots.txt or a 403); the Forum Communications newspapers and MinnPost (their robots.txt turns Claude away). One Forum article was opened with the reading tool before that was noticed; nothing is cited from it.

Republican endorsements: Austin Peterson is listed for MN Senate SD4 on the Clay County Republicans' page headed "Endorsed & Supported Candidates", recorded under endorsed_by as part 0 records the same page, with the page's own two words kept in the unit text for the second reader to judge. None could be recorded for Pam Wolf or Kyle Bragg: mngop.com lists statewide and congressional nominees only, and the Minneapolis Republicans' site names no legislative endorsement (the Becker County Republicans' site names none either). The other party pages read (Carver County Republicans, Senate District 44 DFL, Olmsted County Republicans, Senate District 40 Republicans, Chisago-Isanti DFL, Senate District 19 DFL) name none of this part's candidates.

Balakrishna "Bala" Chintaginjala: Wikipedia's 2020 and 2022 Minnesota Senate election articles list a Bala Chintaginjala in the DFL primaries for Districts 47 and 48. The articles do not name Chanhassen; the tie is the unusual name and a voter guide that lists those runs beside this year's run for mayor. Left for the second reader to judge.
Terri Mallet: the City of Maplewood's Parks and Recreation Commission page lists a member of that name, and the city's 2026 candidate page lists the same name for City Council.
Pam Wolf: the Legislative Reference Library marks her birth date "uncertain"; her campaign site's Experience page gives the same year.

Mary Lewandowski: a voter guide says a St. Cloud LIVE story calls her a former Sartell City Council member, and a 2012 Newsleaders story names a Mary Lewandowski as a past member of that council; the story that would tie the two is on a Forum site and was not read, so nothing is recorded.
Ages given without a year were not turned into birth years (the Elk River Star News gives Mark Swanson's age).

Nothing was found for eight candidates: Justin Ohnstad, Mary Lewandowski, Adam Edward Kasprowicz, Rebecca Carlson, Jonathon Heinonen, Richard Olson, April St. Martin and Aaron Olson. They are listed with no findings. The school districts' own pages show Richard Olson (2024) and April St. Martin (2022 and 2024) ran for the same boards before; those were nonpartisan runs and are not findings.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every url was re-opened with the kit's honest User-Agent (the two austin4mn.com pages also with the reading tool). 55 findings confirmed, 3 removed, 2 reworded. Pam Wolf's birth date stays: the Library's page gives 11/26/1963 (marked uncertain) and her own Experience page says 1963, four days after President Kennedy was assassinated. The Chintaginjala note above no longer has findings behind it.
